hook: Hidden *65 years*. Now it could sell for *$1.6 million*.
dek: One of only seven Patek Philippe Ref. 3452/1 watches ever made headlines Christie's Luxury Week in New York on December 4.
title: The Watch That Kept Two Times: A 65-Year-Old Patek Philippe Heads to Christie's New York
yt_title: Patek Philippe 3452/1: The $1.6M Watch Hidden for 65 Years

slides.label: Hidden
slides.text: For *65 years*, this Patek Philippe never left the family that bought it in *1961*. No catalog. No public appearance.

slides.label: Only 7
slides.text: The *Ref. 3452/1* is one of just *seven* known, and the first of its reference to reach the market since *2006*.

slides.label: Dec 4
slides.text: It headlines Christie's *Important Watches* sale at Rockefeller Center, estimated at *$800K to $1.6M*.

slides.label: The trick
slides.text: Watchmaker *Louis Cottier* made *one movement* drive *two dials*. One heartbeat, two clocks.

slides.label: The look
slides.text: Twin gold-ringed dials, a *39mm* white and yellow gold case and a woven *two-tone* bracelet. No two of the seven match.

slides.label: Also on the block
slides.text: An *Audemars Piguet Ref. 5514*, one of 20 made, and a *"Cherry Logo" Rolex Daytona* fresh from its first family.

slides.label: Our take
slides.text: A dual time watch describes a life: one hand on *home*, the other on the life being *built here*.

slides.label: Front row
slides.text: The Den is inside Christie's *Dec 3 and 4*: the preview, a specialist sit-down and the moment the *hammer falls*.

question: What would you pass down to your kids?

caption_linkedin:
A watch that never left one family for 65 years now headlines Christie's Luxury Week in New York.

The Patek Philippe Dual Time Ref. 3452/1, one of seven known, goes to auction on December 4 with an estimate of $800,000 to $1.6 million. Three things stood out to us:

1. Scarcity plus provenance. Seven made, and none of this reference on the market since 2006. A single-family history since 1961 is the kind of story collectors pay for.
2. Engineering as the differentiator. Louis Cottier made one movement drive two time zones, a cleaner answer than the two-movement designs of the era.
3. Heirlooms are wealth. Before it is a lot number, it is something a parent passed down with a story attached.

The Innovators Den will cover the December 3 press preview and the December 4 sale from inside Christie's New York.
